salient_findings: Hypoechogenic subcardial mass on the posterior gastric wall
Recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site after resection
key_facts: Tumour located below the esophagogastric junction
Presented with melena and progressive anemia
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed a 70 × 50 × 55 mm hypoechogenic mass
Lesion was resected endoscopically by a piecemeal technique under general anesthesia
Recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site six weeks after resection

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent bleeding submucosal gastric tumour with significant size and rapid recurrence

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Initial histopathology confirmed a lipoma, but recurrence raises concern for malignant transformation

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal location and significant size increase suspicion for a smooth muscle tumour

shortlist.label: Glomus tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent bleeding and submucosal location are consistent with a vascular tumour

shortlist.label: Carcinoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Neuroendocrine features and submucosal location make this a plausible, albeit less common, diagnosis

raw.rationale: The tumour's location below the esophagogastric junction, its submucosal nature, and its tendency to bleed and recur despite resection are more consistent with a gastrointestinal stromal tumor than a benign lipoma, especially given the large size and aggressive behavior

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Liposarcomas are rare in the gastrointestinal tract and the initial diagnosis of lipoma may have been incorrect or incomplete

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: While possible, leiomyosarcomas are less common than GISTs in this location and the description does not specifically suggest smooth muscle origin

rejected.label: Glomus tumor
rejected.why: Glomus tumors are typically smaller and located in the distal stomach or small intestine, and are less likely to present with such significant bleeding

rejected.label: Carcinoid tumor
rejected.why: Carcinoid tumors are neuroendocrine in origin and usually have a different presentation, often with hormonal symptoms or smaller, more multifocal lesions

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: The initial diagnosis of lipoma is questionable given the tumour's aggressive behavior, large size, and recurrence
